plain: In November 2004 a Navy fighter pilot, Commander David Fravor, was flying with the group of ships around the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz off San Diego, California. According to his account, he saw the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells it again and again, always stressing Fravor's impression that the thing seemed conscious, almost breathing, and seemed to know he was looking at it. Michels also says it climbed to 80,000 feet and was picked up on radar by the USS Princeton, a ship in the group, crediting this to former Pentagon official Lue Elizondo. Others add names: a guest, Merrick von Renenamp, lists fellow participants Alex Dietrich, Jim Slaight and Kevin Day, and Michels adds pilot Chad Underwood and stresses how carefully the radar data was handled. A veteran researcher, Jacques Vallee, asks why such an object would let eleven F-18 fighter jets chase it all over the Pacific. A former intelligence research director, Eric Haseltine, says something real is going on because so many separate sensors and reluctant witnesses caught it. If true, it would mean Navy pilots met a craft that outflew their jets and seemed aware of them.
